Nafe Singh And Ors vs State Of Haryana And Ors on 7
November, 2024

Author: G.S. Sandhawalia
Bench: G.S. Sandhawalia
 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:146420-DB
 In The High Court Of Punjab & Haryana

 Vs.
State Of Haryana And Ors. .....Respondents

 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Deepak Gupta
Present: Mr. B.S. Rathee, Advocate for the petitioners.

High Court Of Punjab & Haryana
 At Chandigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Mr. Ankur Mittal, Addl. Ag, Haryana and
 Mr. Saurabh Mago, Dag, Haryana.
G.S. Sandhawalia, J. (Oral)

The challenge herein is to the acquisition proceedings initiated vide notification dated 20.10.2001 (Annexure P2) issued under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 [for short 'the Act'] and subsequent notification dated 18.10.2002 (Annexure P3) issued under Section 6 of the Act and award dated 14.10.2004 (Annexure P4).
2.

The land measuring 9 kanals 17 marlas is situated in the revenue estate of village Sultanpur,
Tehsil and District Sonepat and was acquired without any contest.
No protest had been made after the award had been passed in the year 2004.

The writ petition was filed in the year 2014 on the strength of lapse of acquisition proceedings under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Initially, the Writ Petition was disposed of way back on 27.10.2016 in terms of the order passed in CWP- 11445-2008 titled Ghasitu Ram Vs. State of Haryana and others, by 1 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:146420-DB Coordinate Bench of this Court, wherein no reply had been filed,

sentences.text: however, on instructions from the officials, the State counsel had acknowledged the fact that the petitioners have not received the compensation which is still lying with the Land Acquisition Collector.
The Apex Court has now remanded the matter back in Civil Appeal No.2452 of 2024 decided on 12.02.2024 (Annexure R1).

The matter, therefore, in the light of the said judgment of the Apex Court is now before this Court with clarification by the Apex Court that all contentions are kept open to be raised by both the parties as may be legally permissible.

3. In the present petition, reply has been filed by the State submitting that no objection under Section 5A of the Act has been filed by the petitioners and the land of the petitioners was vacant at the time of issuance of notification under the Act.

It is submitted that an amount of `21,32,61,495/-
the award amount was deposited, out of which `17,11,91,909 had already been disbursed among the landowners and rest of amount of compensation of `4,20,69,586/- is lying deposited in the account of LAC.

The Rapat Roznamcha No.235 dated 14.10.2004 was entered regarding taking of the physical possession of the land by the petitioners in accordance with the award, and therefore,
acquisition proceedings are not violated in terms of judgment passed by the Constitution Bench in Indore Development Authority Vs. Manohar Lal and others, AIR 2020 SC 1496 and the land is required for planned development.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority Vs. Manohar Lal and others, AIR 2020 SC 1496
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The lay out plan showing the essentiality of the land is annexed as Annexure R2, which reads as under:-
"That it is submitted the land of petitioners site effect 24 mtr. road, 12 mtr. wide road 1 kanal 4 plots, convenant shopping centre, 6 marla 9 plots, 8 2 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:146420-DB marla 11 plots and school site as per revised layout cum demarcation plan of sector-5 Sonepat.

The copy of the Lay out plan is annexed as Annexure R-2."
4.
We have also perused the site plan, which goes on to show the land as such is essentiality needed for the development which is to be launched for shopping site area which is to be carved out.
In such circumstance, the need as such, can be inferred qua the essentiality of the land.

The petitioners have sought challenge solely on the ground of lapsing of the acquisition proceedings and not having been challenged the issue of acquisition proceedings which were initiated in the year 2001, nothing else survives for consideration.
Resultantly, we do not find any reasons to interfere as such in the matter.
5. The present petition is accordingly dismissed.
(G.S. SANDHAWALIA) JUDGE (DEEPAK GUPTA) 07.11.2024
